governanceNotes: D1 batch 66 (2026-09-26): one bounded association edge authored - optic-atrophy to visual-impairment (rank 1) - classified ASSOCIATION_ONLY with etiologicalConsensus NOT_ESTABLISHED, vaNexusProbabilityAlignment NOT_ASSERTED, and hypothesizedOnly:true. The proposition rests on the 155-eye non-glaucomatous optic atrophy cohort (48.4% at counting-fingers vision or worse; PMID 42293699) and the 220-field chronic Leber archetypal perimetry analysis (total-loss archetype 30%, concentrated in acuity non-recovery; PMID 42390170).

Counter-evidence and caveat screens recorded 2026-09-26: (i) structural-endpoint boundary - optic atrophy is the end-state of prior optic neuropathy, so the edge carries functional consequence rather than active-disease progression and the glaucoma and hypotension visual-impairment windows keep their own evidence (ME-29); (ii) measure non-equivalence - the Leber analysis shows acuity recovery and field damage are not transposable, so visual-impairment claims cannot rest on acuity alone; (iii) etiologic mix - the acuity cohort pools ischemic, traumatic, toxic, compressive, inflammatory, and hereditary causes with severity varying by etiology (toxic poorest); (iv) semantic boundary - acquired dyschromatopsia was NOT authored as color-blindness despite documented color dysfunction in optic neuropathy families (constitutive-feature and congenital-identity mismatch); (v) chronic-stage sampling - both anchors assess established atrophy, so incident-impairment rates are unquantified.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Non-glaucomatous optic atrophy documents visual acuity and field impairment at tertiary-cohort and machine-learning perimetry level: the cross-sectional study of 155 eyes of 155 patients with confirmed non-glaucomatous optic atrophy found 48.4 percent with best-corrected visual acuity of counting-fingers vision or worse (>= 1.90 logMAR), with toxic etiology poorest (5 of 6 cases) and longer duration from symptom onset the sole independent predictor of poorer current acuity (PMID 42293699), and the archetypal analysis of 220 visual fields from 117 molecularly confirmed chronic Leber hereditary optic neuropathy patients found a total-loss field archetype accounting for 30 percent of fields with total-loss patterns significantly concentrated in patients who never recovered acuity (PMID 42390170); recorded as documented association only.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation is established for any individual: optic atrophy is a structural endpoint of prior optic neuropathy and visual dysfunction is its functional consequence, but the located anchors quantify cross-sectional and chronic-stage impairment without untreated comparators, so whether any individual visual impairment is attributable to the atrophy requires individual neuro-ophthalmologic attribution with refractive, retinal, and media-opacity exclusion.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: Retinal ganglion cell axon loss with retrograde degeneration and optic disc pallor drives reduced afferent transmission so diminished visual acuity and field sensitivity result, the axon-loss route consistent with the acuity distribution in the non-glaucomatous optic atrophy cohort and the total-loss field archetypes concentrated in non-recovered chronic hereditary optic neuropathy, but whether this route produced any individual visual impairment remains hypothesized until imaging and perimetry records are reviewed.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: The association is supported at single cross-sectional tertiary cohort plus retrospective machine-learning perimetry analysis class only: the acuity cohort is descriptive from one referral center with no control arm, the field analysis is confined to one hereditary etiology (Leber) at chronic stage, and acuity recovery and field damage were found to be not fully transposable so the two outcome measures cannot be collapsed.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: The acuity cohort is cross-sectional from one tertiary referral center with etiologic mix (ischemic 29.7 percent, traumatic 23.9 percent, toxic, compressive, inflammatory) so pooled impairment rates are not etiology-generalizable; the field analysis covers only chronic Leber hereditary optic neuropathy and shows acuity and field outcomes are not interchangeable; duration of symptoms confounds severity attribution; and refractive error, amblyopia, cataract, macular and retinal disease, and glaucoma compete for individual attribution.
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: glaucomatous optic neuropathy and its own visual-impairment window (the published glaucoma visual-impairment window, not recycled per ME-29)
transient ischemic or hypoperfusion visual symptoms versus fixed impairment (the published hypotension visual-impairment window, not recycled per ME-29)

evidenceGaps: The acuity cohort is cross-sectional from one tertiary referral center with etiologic mix (ischemic 29.7 percent, traumatic 23.9 percent, toxic, compressive, inflammatory) so pooled impairment rates are not etiology-generalizable; the field analysis covers only chronic Leber hereditary optic neuropathy and shows acuity and field outcomes are not interchangeable; duration of symptoms confounds severity attribution; and refractive error, amblyopia, cataract, macular and retinal disease, and glaucoma compete for individual attribution.
suggestions.rationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY at cross-sectional cohort plus perimetry-analysis class with the structural-endpoint and etiologic-mix limits carried openly: the 155-eye non-glaucomatous optic atrophy cohort found 48.4 percent at counting-fingers vision or worse with symptom-duration as the sole independent severity predictor (PMID 42293699) and the chronic Leber archetypal field analysis found total-loss patterns in 30 percent of fields concentrated in non-recovered eyes (PMID 42390170); because the anchors are cross-sectional and chronic-stage without untreated comparators and span mixed etiologies, the conservative standard keeps the edge at association only and routes individual claims through dated neuro-ophthalmologic assessment with refractive, retinal, glaucomatous, and media-opacity exclusion.

sourceReferences.citation: Sharifi M, Zand A, Sharifi M, et al. Etiologic spectrum and predictors of visual acuity in non-glaucomatous optic atrophy SAGE Open Med. 2026;14:20503121261461345. PMID 42293699.
sourceReferences.note: Descriptive cross-sectional study of 155 eyes of 155 patients with confirmed non-glaucomatous optic atrophy (SAGE Open Med 2026, tertiary referral center): 48.4% with BCVA >= 1.90 logMAR (counting fingers or worse); ischemic causes most prevalent (29.7%, 45 NAION), traumatic 23.9%; toxic etiology poorest (5/6 >= 1.90 logMAR); duration from symptom onset sole independent predictor of current acuity (beta 0.253, P=0.010); supports the bounded cross-sectional acuity-impairment association only.

sourceReferences.citation: Coutinho CP, Zanchetta F, Carbonelli M, et al. Archetypal Visual Field Analysis of Patients With Chronic Leber Hereditary Optic Neuropathy in Relation to Visual Recovery Invest Ophthalmol Vis Sci. 2026 Jul 1;67(8):8. PMID 42390170.
sourceReferences.note: Retrospective archetypal machine-learning analysis of 220 visual fields (220 eyes, 117 patients) with molecularly confirmed chronic Leber hereditary optic neuropathy >= 3 years after onset (Invest Ophthalmol Vis Sci 2026): seven field archetypes, total-loss pattern 30% of fields and normal 23%; total-loss archetype significantly more prevalent in the acuity-not-recovered group; acuity recovery and field damage not transposable; supports the bounded chronic-stage field-impairment association only.
